title: Sordland/Turn04/PSnW_EducationReform
description: Ciara reacts to the funding choice and brings up the question of education reform. She proposes a new system to change the old outdated and political education characteristics in the Sordish Education Services. Galade joins the meeting due to the political effects of a change of education. Ciara defends her personal ambitions to the bitter end. The player must make a choice.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "Lucian was seated across from me at..."
entries.dialogueText: Lucian was seated across from me at the table, going through documents. Ciara entered the room.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "We were still in Leiren, staying at..."
entries.dialogueText: We were still in Leiren, staying at a modest guesthouse for state employees. Ciara set up a meeting with me and Lucian to go over her plans for education reform after our school visit.

entries.speaker: Ciara Walda
entries.title: Ciara Walda: "“After the visit yesterday, I could..."
entries.dialogueText: “After the visit yesterday, I couldn't even sleep thinking about that little boy and girl.”

entries.speaker: Ciara Walda
entries.title: Ciara Walda: "“I have never been more sure of my..."
entries.dialogueText: “I have never been more sure of my intentions to reform our education system.”

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "Lucian took off his reading glasses..."
entries.dialogueText: Lucian took off his reading glasses and put it on the table.

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“I agree. An educational reform is..."
entries.dialogueText: “I agree. An educational reform is necessary.”
entries.menuText: “I agree. An educational reform is necessary.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“I don't see what's wrong with our..."
entries.dialogueText: “I don't see what's wrong with our education system.”
entries.menuText: “I don't see what's wrong with our education system.”

entries.speaker: Ciara Walda
entries.title: Ciara Walda: "“You don't?”"
entries.dialogueText: “You don't?”

entries.speaker: Ciara Walda
entries.title: Ciara Walda: "“Can't you look at it objectively a..."
entries.dialogueText: “Can't you look at it objectively and see what's wrong with it? You can't be serious.”

entries.speaker: Lucian Galade
entries.title: Lucian Galade: "“Ciara. Check your tone.”"
entries.dialogueText: “Ciara. Check your tone.”

entries.speaker: Ciara Walda
entries.title: Ciara Walda: ""Would you say that to a man, Lucia..."
entries.dialogueText: "Would you say that to a man, Lucian?”

entries.speaker: Ciara Walda
entries.title: Ciara Walda: "“Those students have to repeat that..."
entries.dialogueText: “Those students have to repeat that same Sollist propaganda every single day. They are being brainwashed at an age when their minds need to be free.”

entries.speaker: Ciara Walda
entries.title: Ciara Walda: "“Exactly.”"
entries.dialogueText: “Exactly.”

entries.speaker: Ciara Walda
entries.title: Ciara Walda: "“Those students have to repeat that..."
entries.dialogueText: “Those students have to repeat that same Sollist propaganda every single day. They are being brainwashed at an age when their minds need to be free.”

entries.speaker: Ciara Walda
entries.title: Ciara Walda: "“On top of that, young girls are de..."
entries.dialogueText: “On top of that, young girls are denied the same opportunity as boys. They're forced into the role of housewife before they even reach puberty!"

entries.speaker: Ciara Walda
entries.title: Ciara Walda: "“On top of that, young girls are de..."
entries.dialogueText: “On top of that, young girls are denied the same opportunity as boys. They're forced into the role of housewife before they even reach puberty! Nothing's changed since I went to school."

entries.speaker: Ciara Walda
entries.title: Ciara Walda: "“Mr. President. We need to bring ch..."
entries.dialogueText: “Mr. President. We need to bring change. We need to free the minds of these young people. They are our future.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“Very well. What do we need to do f..."
entries.dialogueText: “Very well. What do we need to do for an education reform?”
entries.menuText: “Very well. What do we need to do for an education reform?”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“Everything is fine as it is. Why c..."
entries.dialogueText: “Everything is fine as it is. Why change it?”
entries.menuText: “Everything is fine as it is. Why change it?”

entries.speaker: Ciara Walda
entries.title: Ciara Walda: "“I don't think my words are getting..."
entries.dialogueText: “I don't think my words are getting through to you.”

entries.speaker: Ciara Walda
entries.title: Ciara Walda: "“Are you really fine with filling t..."
entries.dialogueText: “Are you really fine with filling the heads of our children with Sollist propaganda? With teaching girls like Deana that their only value to this country is as vessels for childbearing?"

entries.speaker: Ciara Walda
entries.title: Ciara Walda: "“You know the words of Artor S. Wis..."
entries.dialogueText: “You know the words of Artor S. Wisci. You know them better than I do.”

entries.speaker: Ciara Walda
entries.title: Ciara Walda: "“Education is the premise of progre..."
entries.dialogueText: “Education is the premise of progress, in all societies, in all families.”

entries.speaker: Ciara Walda
entries.title: Ciara Walda: "“We need to reform our education sy..."
entries.dialogueText: “We need to reform our education system. Otherwise, Sordland's future is bleak.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“We have more important matters to..."
entries.dialogueText: “We have more important matters to think about than education for a bunch of kids.”
entries.menuText: “We have more important matters to think about than education for a bunch of kids.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“We will not stray away from Soll's..."
entries.dialogueText: “We will not stray away from Soll's path.”
entries.menuText: “We will not stray away from Soll's path.”

entries.speaker: Ciara Walda
entries.title: Ciara Walda: "“I can't believe it. This will be s..."
entries.dialogueText: “I can't believe it. This will be seen as a huge mistake when people look back.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“You have a point. Alright. So what..."
entries.dialogueText: “You have a point. Alright. So what's your plan?”
entries.menuText: “You have a point. Alright. So what's your plan?”

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "Ciara slumped in defeat."
entries.dialogueText: Ciara slumped in defeat.

entries.speaker: Ciara Walda
entries.title: Ciara Walda: "“I'm glad you have seen reason.”"
entries.dialogueText: “I'm glad you have seen reason.”

entries.speaker: Ciara Walda
entries.title: Ciara Walda: "“This is actively poisoning young b..."
entries.dialogueText: “This is actively poisoning young bright minds. Instead of thinking for themselves, they're learning to take things at face value.”

entries.speaker: Ciara Walda
entries.title: Ciara Walda: "“We also need to ensure boys and gi..."
entries.dialogueText: “We also need to ensure boys and girls receive the same instruction. Handcrafts like knitting and sewing should be taught to both sexes, or not at all."

entries.speaker: Ciara Walda
entries.title: Ciara Walda: "“We need to keep politics out of th..."
entries.dialogueText: “We need to keep politics out of the curriculum. Soll should only be viewed as a historical figure. Children shouldn't have to repeat his name everyday.”

entries.speaker: Ciara Walda
entries.title: Ciara Walda: "“Sordland's youth must be technical..."
entries.dialogueText: “Sordland's youth must be technically skilled and capable for the next decade. That won't be possible with the amount of nationalistic indoctrination and narrow-minded thinking found in schools today.”

entries.speaker: Ciara Walda
entries.title: Ciara Walda: "“Either we raise a generation ready..."
entries.dialogueText: “Either we raise a generation ready for the challenges of the future or not. What will it be, Mr. President?”

entries.speaker: Lucian Galade
entries.title: Lucian Galade: "“As much as I respect Colonel Soll,..."
entries.dialogueText: “As much as I respect Colonel Soll, his time has passed. Now is our time. I do think this might be the first step of a larger plan.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“Lucian, what do you think?”"
entries.dialogueText: “Lucian, what do you think?”
entries.menuText: “Lucian, what do you think?”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“Maintain the traditional education..."
entries.dialogueText: “Maintain the traditional education system.”
entries.menuText: “Maintain the traditional education system.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“Reform the education system.”"
entries.dialogueText: “Reform the education system.”
entries.menuText: “Reform the education system.”

entries.speaker: Ciara Walda
entries.title: Ciara Walda: "“You will not regret it. I will get..."
entries.dialogueText: “You will not regret it. I will get to work immediately.”

entries.speaker: Ciara Walda
entries.title: Ciara Walda: "“I am utterly disappointed. Especia..."
entries.dialogueText: “I am utterly disappointed. Especially after yesterday's school visit. I thought it would awaken something in you.”

entries.speaker: Ciara Walda
entries.title: Ciara Walda: "“It will be an uphill battle, consi..."
entries.dialogueText: “It will be an uphill battle, considering that the education budget was lowered against my recommendations. But I will give it my best.”

entries.speaker: Lucian Galade
entries.title: Lucian Galade: "“Now that the decision was made, le..."
entries.dialogueText: “Now that the decision was made, let's move on.”

entries.speaker: Ciara Walda
entries.title: Ciara Walda: "“After the budget increase, the min..."
entries.dialogueText: “After the budget increase, the ministry quickly began formulating plans on how to effectively use the money.”

entries.speaker: Ciara Walda
entries.title: Ciara Walda: "“With no change in budget, the mini..."
entries.dialogueText: “With no change in budget, the ministry was left to its own devices. We made some tough choices but still lack additional funds.”

entries.speaker: Ciara Walda
entries.title: Ciara Walda: "“So, what is your decision?”"
entries.dialogueText: “So, what is your decision?”

entries.speaker: Ciara Walda
entries.title: Ciara Walda: "“But before moving forward, the que..."
entries.dialogueText: “But before moving forward, the question of keeping education fully state-funded or allowing for new private schools remains open.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“Education should remain as a state..."
entries.dialogueText: “Education should remain as a state service only. Certainly this is the most ideal situation.”
entries.menuText: “Education should remain as a state service only. Certainly this is the most ideal situation.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“There is a possibility of privatiz..."
entries.dialogueText: “There is a possibility of privatization having negative side effects.”
entries.menuText: “There is a possibility of privatization having negative side effects.”

entries.speaker: Ciara Walda
entries.title: Ciara Walda: "“Trust me, I know that. It could in..."
entries.dialogueText: “Trust me, I know that. It could increase the cost of a quality education, but that is hardly avoidable now anyway.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“Tell us about the benefits of allo..."
entries.dialogueText: “Tell us about the benefits of allowing private schools.”
entries.menuText: “Tell us about the benefits of allowing private schools.”

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "Ciara skimmed over her documents be..."
entries.dialogueText: Ciara skimmed over her documents before continuing.

entries.speaker: Ciara Walda
entries.title: Ciara Walda: "“This has led us to think about all..."
entries.dialogueText: “This has led us to think about allowing privatization to at least keep vital education services unaffected.”

entries.speaker: Ciara Walda
entries.title: Ciara Walda: "“Therefore we are investigating if..."
entries.dialogueText: “Therefore we are investigating if privatizing education would draw enough funds to conduct investments.”

entries.speaker: Ciara Walda
entries.title: Ciara Walda: "“It would be a lie to say that a de..."
entries.dialogueText: “It would be a lie to say that a decrease in the budget didn't force us to consider this. We just need the funds even though we don't like privatization.”

entries.speaker: Ciara Walda
entries.title: Ciara Walda: "“We can manage without additional f..."
entries.dialogueText: “We can manage without additional funds. The only reason I wanted to consider it is to have more money to improve education.”

entries.speaker: Ciara Walda
entries.title: Ciara Walda: "“We have enough money to improve ed..."
entries.dialogueText: “We have enough money to improve education in Sordland. We do not need to complicate things further with a privatization incentive.”

entries.speaker: Ciara Walda
entries.title: Ciara Walda: "“I've made my opinion clear: I'm ag..."
entries.dialogueText: “I've made my opinion clear: I'm against it. But it would give us additional funds for education while increasing competition.”

entries.speaker: Ciara Walda
entries.title: Ciara Walda: "“I agree. The government should be..."
entries.dialogueText: “I agree. The government should be responsible of managing education completely.”

entries.speaker: Lucian Galade
entries.title: Lucian Galade: "“State education is contrary to our..."
entries.dialogueText: “State education is contrary to our overall economic strategy of promoting a market economy.”

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "A few minutes of deliberation passe..."
entries.dialogueText: A few minutes of deliberation passed.

entries.speaker: Ciara Walda
entries.title: Ciara Walda: "“There aren't many. But it would gi..."
entries.dialogueText: “There aren't many. But it would give us sorely needed funds and increase competition among schools.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“What are the advantages of privati..."
entries.dialogueText: “What are the advantages of privatization?"
entries.menuText: “What are the advantages of privatization?"

entries.speaker: Lucian Galade
entries.title: Lucian Galade: "“Private education is inconsistent..."
entries.dialogueText: “Private education is inconsistent with our overall economic strategy of a planned economy.”

entries.speaker: Lucian Galade
entries.title: Lucian Galade: "“It would go against our overall ec..."
entries.dialogueText: “It would go against our overall economic strategy of a planned economy.”

entries.speaker: Ciara Walda
entries.title: Ciara Walda: "“The reduction of the education bud..."
entries.dialogueText: “The reduction of the education budget left our hands completely tied. We are in a budget crisis management situation.”

entries.speaker: Lucian Galade
entries.title: Lucian Galade: "“It would support our overall econo..."
entries.dialogueText: “It would support our overall economic strategy of promoting a market economy.”

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "She let out a deep sigh."
entries.dialogueText: She let out a deep sigh.

entries.speaker: Ciara Walda
entries.title: Ciara Walda: "“Very well.”"
entries.dialogueText: “Very well.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“Initiate privatization to draw mor..."
entries.dialogueText: “Initiate privatization to draw more funds. This should allow for more competition and quality.”
entries.menuText: “Initiate privatization to draw more funds. This should allow for more competition and quality.” [+2 Government Budget]

entries.speaker: Lucian Galade
entries.title: Lucian Galade: "“This has been a very productive da..."
entries.dialogueText: “This has been a very productive day. I will be returning to Holsord.”

entries.speaker: Ciara Walda
Player
entries.title: Player: "“Thank you for your time everybody...."
entries.dialogueText: “Thank you for your time everybody.”
entries.menuText: “Thank you for your time.”

entries.speaker: Ciara Walda
entries.title: Ciara Walda: "“Will do. That should be it for now..."
entries.dialogueText: “Will do. That should be it for now. I will get to work and report back later.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“Keep education solely a matter of..."
entries.dialogueText: “Keep education solely a matter of the state. We need to prevent interference from private interests."
entries.menuText: “Keep education solely a matter of the state. We need to prevent interference from private interests."

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "We dispersed after spending nearly..."
entries.dialogueText: We dispersed after spending nearly the entire day together. I took a moment simply to breathe the fresh evening air of Leiren.

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“Have a good day and safe travels.”"
entries.dialogueText: “Have a good day and safe travels.”
entries.menuText: “Have a good day.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“See you both later.”"
entries.dialogueText: “See you both later.”
entries.menuText: “See you later.”

entries.speaker: Ciara Walda
entries.title: Ciara Walda: "“Great. That should be it for now...."
entries.dialogueText: “Great. That should be it for now. I will get to work and report back later.”

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "I felt calmer here, somehow. But I..."
entries.dialogueText: I felt calmer here, somehow. But I would have to return to the chaos of Holsord soon enough.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "Ciara looked furious. She shook her..."
entries.dialogueText: Ciara looked furious. She shook her head slowly.

entries.speaker: Ciara Walda
entries.title: Ciara Walda: "“The only way people like me, Nia,..."
entries.dialogueText: “The only way people like me, Nia, Lileas, Gloria, even your wife were able to escape that is because our families were fortunate and well-connected enough to be able to educate us outside of the public school system. Is that the kind of country you want your daughter to grow up in?"

entries.speaker: Ciara Walda
entries.title: Ciara Walda: "“Women like me, Lileas, Nia, even y..."
entries.dialogueText: “Women like me, Lileas, Nia, even your wife -- we had to study twice as hard to receive the same university education that you and Lucian took for granted. Is that the kind of country you want your daughter to grow up in?"
